Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/ 6 24. In the case of Jasbir Kaur Sehgal (Smt.) v. District Judge, Dehradun & Others, reported at (1997) 7 Supreme Court Cases 7, it has been held as under: "8. The wife has no fixed abode of residence. She says she is living in a Gurudwara with her eldest daughter for safety. On the other hand the husband has sufficient income and a house to himself. She is aggrieved only because of the paltry amount of maintenance fixed by the courts. Court CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs, capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate. In the circumstances of the present case we fix maintenance pendente lite at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per month payable by respondent-husband to the appellant-wife." 25. Their lordship of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Bharat Hegde v. Saroj Hegde, (140 (2007) DLT 16, had culled out following 11 factors, which can be taken into consideration for deciding the application under Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act, relevant portion of which reads as under: "8. Unfortunately, in India, parties do not truthfully reveal their income. For self employed persons or persons employed in the unorganized sector, truthful income never surfaces. Tax avoidance is the norm. Tax compliance is the exception in this country. The court has to take a general view. The same are: (1) Status of the parties. (2) Reasonable wants of the claimant. (10) The non-applicant to defray the cost of litigation. 23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Jasbir Kaur (Smt.) (supra), has also recognized the fact that spouses in the proceedings for maintenance do not truthfully disclose their true income and therefore some guess work on the part of the Court is permissible. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court has also observed that "considering the diverse claims made by the parties one inflating the income and the other suppressing an element of conjecture and guess work does enter for arriving at the income of the husband. It cannot be done by any mathematical precision". 26. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Neeta Rakesh Jain v. Rakesh Jeetmal Jain reported at AIR 2010 SC 3540, has laid guidelines which the courts may keep in mind at the time of fixing the quantum of maintenance. "In other words, in the matter of making an order for interim maintenance, the discretion of the court must be guided by the criterion provided in the Section, namely, the means of the parties and also after taking into account incidental and other relevant factors like social status; the background from which both the parties come from and the economical dependence of the petitioner. Since their lordship of High Court of Delhi in case Annurita Vohra vs. Sandeep Vohra 2004 (74) DRJ 99 had laid down the guidelines regarding the quantum of maintenance, so, taking into consideration the fact that the respondent (herein) is having one minor child, who is also living under care and custody of respondent (herein), the Ld. Trial Court was required to grant Rs.5,000/- Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/ 8 per month each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child, but, the Ld. Trial Court after assessing the monthly income of the appellant (herein) as Rs.20,000/- per month, has granted Rs.6,500/- each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child. and thus, the amount of maintenance awarded by the Ld. Trial Court is modified in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case "Annurita Vohra vs. Sandeep Vohra, 2004 (74) DRJ 99".
